name: Tabs
summary: A row of buttons over a box of content is the easiest thing on a page to draw and one of the easiest to get wrong. The pattern hands the arrow keys a job the Tab key used to do, so the whole strip becomes one stop — and the panel underneath still has to be somewhere the keyboard can land.
demoNote: Examples 2 to 5 are live. Example 2 asks the browser which elements it will really give focus to and prints every stop three strips have; example 3 counts the panels opened while arrowing across; example 4 names the next thing Tab reaches after the selected tab; example 5 puts a row of links wearing role=tab beside the same links in a nav.

contract.useWhen: Swap panels in place. Not for moving between pages; that is jump-nav.
keyboard: move and select, since the panels are already in the DOM
the same, and the only pair that moves, when the strip is vertical
one stop for the strip, then into the panel
states: vertical — aria-orientation=vertical on the tablist, which swaps which arrows move
failureModes: every tab at tabindex=0, so the strip is as many stops as it has tabs
unselected panels hidden with opacity, which hides them from nobody — their links are still stops
no tabindex on the panel, so Tab steps over it and its name is never read
links wearing role=tab, announcing as a widget while aria-controls names panels nobody built
api: AC.createTabs(root, options) -> { select, selected, tabs, panels, destroy }
